html:
The Pisamira are one of the smallest Indigenous peoples of Colombia, a few dozen people living on the Vaupés River near the Brazilian border. Their language belongs to the Eastern branch of the Tucanoan family and is very close to Tucano, the main trade language of the Vaupés.

Like their neighbours, such as the Waíkhana, they follow the custom of the region that people marry someone who speaks a different language. They live by fishing and farming bitter manioc, in a region hit hard by the rubber trade and by missions in the 1900s.
